body.heading: Feel first
paragraphs: Walk slowly with your adult and find three trees. Touch each trunk gently with your fingertips. One might feel rough, one might feel smooth, and one might feel bumpy like a dragon's back.
Bark is the tree's coat. It keeps the tree safe from weather and bugs. Every kind of tree wears a slightly different coat.

body.heading: Make a rubbing
paragraphs: Hold your paper flat against the trunk. Your adult can help hold the top. Rub the side of a crayon over the paper, up and down, until the bark's pattern appears like magic.
Try the same tree with two colours. Then rub a different tree and compare. Which rubbing has long lines? Which one has little cracks and dots?

body.heading: Be a bark detective
paragraphs: Look at your rubbings together. Can you guess which tree each one came from? Show your adult and see if they can guess too.
Thank the trees by leaving them just as you found them. Take your rubbings home, but leave the bark and branches exactly as they were.

takeaway: Every tree's bark has its own pattern, and a crayon rubbing lets you take the pattern home without harming the tree.
materials: Thick crayons with the paper peeled off
A bag for collecting fallen leaves
safetyNotes: Stay where an adult can see you. Never pull bark off a tree — only rub the surface gently.
screenFreeExtension: Lay your rubbings side by side at home and make a pretend forest on the floor with toy animals.
